summary: This article explains what happens during solar and lunar eclipses, why they do not happen every month, and how to watch them safely.
introduce: Write the key term “align” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “Eclipses of the Sun and Moon” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: to line up in a straight line
only part, not complete or whole
to say what will happen before it happens

challengeTerms.def: the short time when the Sun or Moon is completely covered in an eclipse
leaning to one side; not flat or straight

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that an eclipse is worth staying up late or travelling far to see? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why eclipses do not happen every month, and describe what a person would see during a total solar eclipse.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review align, partial, and predict, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses annular, totality, and tilted to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
